items.item:
7. A complete configuration with variables that name no item —
   `REGISTRY_EXTRA`, `REGISTRY_`, and one without the prefix — starts, and
   none of them appears in a diagnostic or a setting; one where the backup key
   is set as `REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEYY` instead of its own name stops the start,
   naming the backup key as missing; one with three tokens set and the fourth
   misspelt stops the start naming that token; one with only a misspelt
   token and no other token starts owner-only.
   Shows A17-1. [witness: verification:registry_a17_unknown_variables_ignored_misspelt_item_missing]

verdicts.item:
7. A complete configuration with variables that name no item —
   `REGISTRY_EXTRA`, `REGISTRY_`, and one without the prefix — starts, and
   none of them appears in a diagnostic or a setting; one where the backup key
   is set as `REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEYY` instead of its own name stops the start,
   naming the backup key as missing; one with three tokens set and the fourth
   misspelt stops the start naming that token; one with only a misspelt
   token and no other token starts owner-only.
   Shows A17-1. [witness: verification:registry_a17_unknown_variables_ignored_misspelt_item_missing]
quotes: assert diagnostic is not None and _names(diagnostic, "backup_key"), diagnostic
assert name not in diagnostic or name == "REGISTRY_", diagnostic
assert "REGISTRY_EXTRA" not in diagnostic and "KEYY" not in diagnostic
assert diagnostic is not None and _names(diagnostic, "token_cabinet"), diagnostic
verdicts.why: The check verifies that a complete configuration containing all three unknown-variable forms starts and serves, while unknown names and values do not appear in the failure diagnostic. It also verifies that the misspelt backup key and fourth token cause non-serving failures naming the missing items, and that a lone misspelt token produces an owner-only start with no service listener.
